Clacton Airshow

A free seaside air show on the Essex coast

Clacton is one of the friendliest seaside shows in the calendar. You get warbirds, fast jets and display teams out over the North Sea, a pier full of rides just along the front, and in 2026 there was a twilight display on the Thursday evening too. This guide is here to help you plan and organise your days by the sea, and I’ve shared how I would go about it.

WhenThursday 26 and Friday 27 August 2027
EntryFree
ShowgroundWest Greensward, from 11:00 (2026)
StationClacton-on-Sea, about 15 min walk

Last checked 3 November 2026. Where a time or price says 2026, it’s from last year’s show until the 2027 details are out.

2027 confirmedClacton Airshow is confirmed for Thursday 26 and Friday 27 August 2027. When I last checked, the line-up, flying times and travel details hadn’t been announced, so I’ve based those on the 2025 and 2026 shows for now.

The show at a glance

Clacton Airshow runs along the seafront either side of the pier, with the crowd centre on the West Greensward. Tendring District Council puts it on, it’s free to watch, and 2026 was its 33rd year.

What I like about Clacton is that it’s held on a Thursday and Friday at the end of August, so it feels a little calmer than the big weekend seafront shows. The Airshow Village on the West Greensward opens at 11:00, and the flying fills the afternoon on both days, so you have the morning to settle in.

For me, the Thursday is the one to circle. After the afternoon display there’s a twilight display over the sea, with aerobatics, lit up aircraft and pyrotechnics against the seafront. In 2026 there were fireworks at Clacton Pier straight after. If you can only make one day and you don’t mind a later finish, I would suggest the Thursday, and children love to see the lights.

The main things I would plan for are the seafront road closures and parking. I would advise using the Park and Ride or the train, and getting there well before the flying starts, as this has worked for me in the past.

Meet the RAF

In 2026 the RAF Careers Engagement team brought a replica Typhoon cockpit and a Batak reaction challenge to the West Greensward. Children love to have a go, and it’s a nice way for them to learn about the different roles in the RAF. If anyone in your group would like to join, I would suggest it as the place to ask any questions they may have.

At most UK shows the RAF display teams spend time on the ground too, like the Red Arrows pilots and their ground crew, and kids can often get stickers and photos. I would keep an eye out for them in the Airshow Village between displays.

    Do I need a ticket?
    No, watching from the seafront is free. The council asks for donations to help keep the show going, online through the official website or in the bucket collections, and buying the £6 programme helps too.
    Which roads close?
    Roads around the seafront are closed for the show. In 2026 Marine Parade West and Pier Gap were closed for the whole event, and Collingwood Road, St Vincent Road, Nelson Road and Trafalgar Road were residents only parking. I would follow the signs and stewards on the day, allow extra time and not count on parking on the seafront.
    How does the Park and Ride work?
    You park at Clacton Shopping Village on Stephenson Road West and take the bus to the seafront. In 2026 buses ran about every 10 minutes from 10:00 to Marine Parade East, with fares of £6 adult, £5 for ages 5 to 19 or £16 for a group ticket, and no discount for concessionary bus passes. The last bus back left the seafront at 22:00 on the Thursday and 18:30 on the Friday.
    Where do coaches go?
    Coaches drop off at Angle Field, CO15 6PH. In 2026 the advised route was Wash Lane, Freeland Road, Tower Road, Marine Parade and Marine Parade East to Angle Field, then on to Clacton Leisure Centre, Vista Road, CO15 6DB, to park.
    Can I camp on the seafront?
    No. A High Court injunction stops unauthorised camping in the designated seafront areas around the show. In 2026 it ran from Thursday 20 August to Saturday 5 September. I would suggest the campsites and holiday parks in the Where to stay section instead.
    Will I get home after the twilight display?
    On the Thursday the flying carries on into the evening. In 2026 the last Park and Ride bus left the seafront at 22:00. If you’re on the train, I would check the last train back before you set off, and I would advise leaving a little before the very end if your connection is tight.

    Pick Your Day

    Clacton runs on a Thursday and a Friday, and the two days feel quite different. The Thursday goes on into the evening, while the Friday is a straight daytime show. I would think about how late your group can realistically stay, as that usually decides it.

    Dates26 and 27 August 2027
    OpeningFrom 11:00 (2026)
    TwilightThursday in 2026
    EntryFree both days
    ThursdayIn 2026 the site was open 11:00 to 22:00. Afternoon flying with the Red Arrows, then a twilight display with the Desert Spitfire, the Firebirds, the MiG-17 and Otto the Helicopter’s pyrotechnics, and fireworks at Clacton Pier after.
    FridayIn 2026 the site was open 11:00 to 17:00. A full afternoon of flying with the Red Arrows again, and the P-51D Mustang “Moonbeam McSwine” was a Friday only act. You’re heading home in daylight.

    I Would Pick The Thursday

    1. WhyYou get the afternoon flying and then the twilight display, with lit up aircraft and pyrotechnics over the sea. Children love to see it, and in 2026 there were fireworks at the pier to finish.
    2. Good to knowThe twilight display ran in 2026, but when I last checked it hadn’t been confirmed for 2027. I would check before you plan the whole day round it.
    3. Getting thereIn 2026 the last Park and Ride bus left the seafront at 22:00. If you’re on the train, I would look up the last one home before you set off.

    I Would Pick The Friday

    1. WhyIt’s a full afternoon of flying with the Red Arrows, and you’re done by teatime. That might work for your family if little ones flag by late afternoon.
    2. Good to knowIn 2025 the Friday flying started at about 13:00, a little earlier than the Thursday. The 2027 times will be in the programme.
    3. Getting thereIn 2026 the last Park and Ride bus left the seafront at 18:30, so I wouldn’t hang about too long after the last display.
    Jack’s tipIf you can do both, I would go on the Friday for the daytime flying and save the Thursday for a late afternoon arrival, a tea in town and the twilight display. Bring a warm top. It gets cool on the front once the sun goes.

    Help On Show Days

    Clacton is a relaxed show, but it’s still a busy seafront with thousands of people, a twilight display and road closures to think about. Here’s what I would do if something goes wrong, plus quick answers to the questions I see asked most before the show.

    More helpIf the forecast looks grim, have a look at my rainy day plan. If you or someone in your group finds noise and crowds hard, my calm visit guide may help. And for the end of the day, there’s getting home from an airshow.
    In an emergency, call 999. For anything else on the day, I would find the nearest steward or head to the Airshow Village on the West Greensward.

    If Something Goes Wrong

    Lost Each Other

    I would agree a meeting point as soon as you arrive, like the entrance to the pier or the West Greensward toilets. For younger children, I would advise writing your phone number on their wrist. If you can’t find them, please tell a steward straight away. In 2026 there was a free wristband scheme for children, with each part of the seafront given its own colour. I would pick one up for each child from a Beach Patrol office or a steward on arrival. The lost persons points are at the Beach Patrol offices, and the ground crew can help you get there.

    Feeling Unwell

    Tell the nearest steward and they can get help to you. On West Beach the lifeguards give first aid while they’re on duty. In 2026 there were three first aid points, at the Hastings Avenue seafront car park, at Pier Gap and in the centre of the event site, opposite Event Information. There’s very little shade on the seafront, so I would advise drinking plenty.

    Flying Times

    You’ll find the times in the official programme, which is sold on the West Greensward. Timings can change because of the weather or for operational reasons, so I would keep an eye on the official social media.

    Away From The Commentary

    If you’re watching from Martello Bay or the pier, Radio Airshow on Actual Radio carried the commentary in 2026. There’s more in .

    Bad Weather

    Sea mist, low cloud or strong wind can change the programme or stop some displays. I would head for the cafés or the pier for shelter while it passes.

    Loud Displays

    Some displays are very noisy and may upset people who are sensitive to noise. I would advise ear defenders for children.

    Getting Home

    In 2026 the last Park and Ride bus left the seafront at 22:00 on the Thursday and 18:30 on the Friday. I would check yours, and your last train, before the twilight display. Take a look at .

    Finding Your Car

    After the twilight display it’s dark and everyone leaves at once. I would drop a pin on your phone’s map when you park, as it saves a lot of wandering.

    Quick Answers

    Is it free?

    Yes, it’s free to watch from the seafront. Donations online, in the bucket collections or by buying the programme help keep it that way.

    When is it in 2027?

    Thursday 26 and Friday 27 August 2027, on Clacton seafront.

    What time does it start?

    In 2026 the Airshow Village on the West Greensward opened at 11:00, with the flying through the afternoon on both days. The 2027 times should come out nearer the show.

    Is there a twilight display in 2027?

    There was one on the Thursday evening in 2026, but when I last checked it hadn’t been confirmed for 2027. I would advise keeping an eye on the official site.

    How much is the programme?

    It was £6 in 2026, sold on the West Greensward. It’s got the flight times in it, plus some facts about the aircraft.

    Can I bring my dog?

    Dogs aren’t allowed on West Beach from May to September, except guide dogs. On the promenade they need to be on a lead. With the noise, I would think carefully about how your dog will cope.

    Can I have a BBQ on the beach?

    No. Gas barbecues aren’t allowed on West Beach.

    Can I fly my drone?

    No, unauthorised drones aren’t allowed at the event.

    Can I camp on the seafront?

    No. A court injunction stops unauthorised camping on the seafront around the show. Take a look at for campsites nearby.

    Where are the toilets?

    The West Greensward toilets are on Marine Parade Way, with a Changing Places toilet next door. There are also toilets at Pier Gap. There’s more in .

    Are there lifeguards?

    West Beach has lifeguards in the school holidays and at weekends, from 10:30 to 17:30.

    Can I go for a swim?

    Swimming isn’t advised at West Beach, because of the water quality and the groynes and pier. I would stick to paddling, and in 2026 people were asked not to go beyond the water’s edge while the flying was on.

    I don’t have an answer for that here. The official Clacton Airshow site may help.

    The 2027 details may change, so please see the rules before you go.

    The Ground Show

    The flying is in the afternoon, so the ground show is what fills your morning. It all sits in the Airshow Village on the West Greensward, which opened at 11:00 on both days in 2026. There’s very little static aircraft display at Clacton, so think of it more as a seaside festival with an aviation theme.

    WhereWest Greensward
    Opens11:00 (2026)
    CostFree to walk round
    CashNo machines on site
    In 2026

    Replica Typhoon Cockpit

    The RAF Careers Engagement team brought a replica Typhoon cockpit to sit in, along with RAF careers displays. I’ve said more about them in the .

    In 2026

    Batak Reaction Challenge

    A wall of lights you have to hit as fast as you can. Children love to have a go, and it’s harder than it looks.

    In 2026

    STEM Activities

    Hands on science and engineering stands aimed at getting young people thinking about careers in aviation. Worth a look if you have a curious one.

    Bring cash

    Trade Stands And Exhibitors

    In 2026 there were stalls selling everything from natural pet food to handmade garden furniture and handcrafted goods from Indonesia. There are no cash machines on site, so I would bring some with you.

    Pay as you go

    Food Concessions

    Local traders like Whippy Bro’s, Spud Box and Vintage Shakes were serving in 2026, and Combat 2 Coffee was back in the services area. For toilets and sit down meals, take a look at .

    £6 (2026)

    The Official Programme

    The Ground Crew walk the site selling it, and it has the flying times in. I would buy one early so you can plan the afternoon.

    Pay as you go

    Clacton Pier

    Just east of the show, with rides, arcades and food. It’s a handy break if the village gets too busy, and the nearest cash machine is there too.

    How I Would Do It

    1. Save your pitch firstIf you want a front row seat, head to the seafront first and set up your chairs or blanket. The Greensward fills quickly.
    2. Then take a look roundOnce you’re set, walk the village. Visit the RAF stand, speak to any crews you spot, check out the trade stalls and see what food is on.
    3. Toilet before the flyingI would go before the first aircraft appears, as the queues build fast once it starts.
    4. Use the gapsIf you aren’t waiting for a particular display, use it as a toilet or food break. The stalls are much quieter while everyone is looking up.
    Jack’s tipI would head to the RAF stand soon after saving your pitch. It’s quieter before the bulk of the crowds arrive, so children have a better chance of a go in the cockpit without a long wait.

    Exhibitors and attractions change each year, so the 2027 village may look different.

    Pick your spot

    The display line runs along the seafront either side of the pier, with the crowd looking out to sea. The things I would think about are how close you want to be to the crowd centre on the West Greensward, how much space you need and how near you’d like the food and toilets.

    It fills first, so I would arrive early and save your pitch before you look round the stalls.

If you head out towards Holland on Sea or Jaywick, I would park in a proper car park or a legal space, keep driveways and junctions clear, and stay off private gardens and the beach huts. The roads near the seafront are closed on show days, so please follow the signs.

    Clacton Airshow Seafront Information

    Clacton is a seaside show, and that changes how you plan your day. The tide, the groynes, the sea breeze and the mist that can sit over the North Sea all play a part. I’ve put what I’ve learned about the seafront itself in the tabs below.

    Seafront guide

    Three more things to know about the seafront

    Sea Mist And Wind

    A seafront show has its own weather. It can be bright and sunny in town while a bank of mist sits out over the North Sea, right where the aircraft fly. I think it’s worth knowing what to look out for, so a grey morning doesn’t put you off.

    Who Decides?

    Fly or notThe display teams and organisers
    WhenOn the day, display by display
    Latest newsThe official social media
    Why mist forms

    When warm, damp air drifts over the cooler sea, it cools down and turns into mist or fog. It often sits just off the coast while the town stays sunny.

    It can lift quickly

    A misty morning doesn’t always mean a misty afternoon. As the day warms up, the mist often thins or drifts away, so I would suggest staying put rather than giving up early.

    Lower cloud, different show

    Teams like the Red Arrows fly a full looping display when the cloud is high, and a rolling or flat display when it’s lower. You’ll still see them, just flying a different routine.

    The wind off the sea

    Strong or gusty wind can stop some displays, especially lighter historic aircraft. It also makes the beach feel much colder, and it gets cooler still for the twilight display, so I would bring layers.

    Jack’s tipOn a misty day, I would keep an eye on the official social media for any changes, and look out to sea rather than at the sky above you. In my experience the mist is often worse over the water than over the town.

    Please treat this as a general guide rather than an official forecast. For the live weather and a flying conditions check, take a look at .

    Along The Seafront

    Most people watch from the West Greensward or the beach below it, but the show is visible right along the front. Moving away from the crowd centre gives you a very different day, so I would think about who you’re with and how close you want to be.

    Three Other Ways

    EastClacton Pier
    WestTowards Martello Bay
    On the waterCheck the rules first

    From The Pier

    East of the crowd centre, with food, rides and arcades right there. This might work for your family if you want plenty to do between displays, though you’ll be further from the commentary.

    Towards Martello Bay

    West of the Greensward it’s quieter, with more room to spread out. You’ll be further from the crowd centre, so I would suggest tuning into the radio commentary.

    From Your Own Boat

    In 2026 there was a Maritime Safety Zone off the seafront, with a Local Navigation Warning, and boats, jet skis, sailboards and canoes weren’t allowed inside the exclusion zone during the displays. Please keep well clear.

    • Before you goI would get in touch with the council’s Seafronts team and ask about the navigation warning for 2027.
    • In an emergencyCall 999 and ask for the Coastguard.

    Please never go inside the display area, even between displays.

    Boat tripsI haven’t found a confirmed public boat trip to watch the show, so I wouldn’t plan your day around one. If you see one advertised, I would check with the operator that it stays outside the display area.

    For where to watch along the seafront, take a look at .

    Shooting at Clacton

    The crowd looks out to sea, roughly south south east, so you’re shooting into the sun around the middle of the day, and it swings round to your right through the afternoon. By the Thursday twilight display the sun has set behind your right shoulder. Aircraft fly further out than at an airfield, so I have found reach matters more here.

    Get creative over the sea

    Clacton can be a bit of a challenge for photographers. The crowd line faces out to sea and towards the sun for much of the day, so aircraft can look dark against a bright sky, and sea haze can soften detail and flatten the colour. I would suggest using the sun guide to plan when you shoot, adding a little exposure compensation when you are shooting into the sun, and saving your close up work for later in the afternoon, when the light swings round behind you.

    Ideas to try

    • I would wait for the banking passes. A topside or underside view shows far more of the aircraft than a straight flypast.
    • Try leaving room in the frame for smoke trails, so they lead the eye to the aircraft.
    • I like to zoom out now and then to include the pier, the beach or the crowds on the Greensward, so the photo says Clacton.
    • On the Thursday evening, I would try a slower shutter for the twilight display, so the aircraft lights and pyrotechnics leave trails.

    Starting settings

    Pick what’s flying and the weather, and I’ll give you a starting point. It uses 1/1250 as a benchmark for the fastest shutter, at least double your focal length, and keeps ISO at 1200 or below, so the files stay clean and the shutter stays realistic for the subject. I would check your histogram after the first pass and adjust from there.

    Kids’ Corner

    I think Clacton is a brilliant first air show for children. There’s golden sand, the pier with its rides and arcades, and aircraft roaring low over the sea. The flying is in the afternoon, so I would suggest giving them a mission for the morning. Here’s a seaside spotting card they can tick off as they go.

    Spotter’s mission

    The line up changes each day and with the weather, so please don’t worry if you can’t spot them all on your visit.

    Making The Day Easier

    It’s free

    There are no tickets to buy for the kids, so the only things you really need to pay for are the programme and parking.

    Ear defenders

    Some displays are very loud, so I would advise ear defenders for babies and toddlers, especially for the fast jets. Your child’s ears are delicate, so try to protect them as much as possible.

    The pier

    Rides, arcades and food just east of the show. Children love it, and I would suggest it for filling the time before the flying starts.

    Sun and shade

    There’s very little shade on the seafront, so I would pack sun cream, hats and plenty of water.

    Bucket and spade

    West Beach is golden sand, so I would pack a bucket and spade to keep little ones busy between displays.

    Toilets

    The West Greensward toilets and the Changing Places toilet are close by. Take a look at .

    Jack’s tipIf you’re staying for the twilight display, I would suggest bringing a warm top and a torch for the walk back. Little ones will be tired, so I would plan where you’re heading before it gets dark.

    Keep The Show Free

    Clacton is free to watch, but it costs a lot to put on. The council asks visitors to chip in where they can, and I think it’s worth doing if you’ve had a good day. Even a few pounds in a bucket helps keep it going.

    Buy The Programme

    The money goes straight back into the show. In 2026 you could buy one from the Ground Crew on site, the Visitor Information Centre, Clacton station, the Beach Patrol office or Clacton Pier.

    Any amount

    There are bucket collections around the show. I would keep some change in your pocket, as there are no cash machines on the site.

    If you don’t carry cash, you can give through the official website before or after the show. This may work for you if you’re watching from home on the radio too.

    Local firms can sponsor a display or take an advert in the programme. In 2026 adverts started at £250 plus VAT for a quarter page.

    Food, toilets & access

    One thing I really like about Clacton over airfield shows is that a whole town sits right behind the display line. You can eat in the Airshow Village, bring a picnic, or step back into town for a sit down meal, whichever suits your family.

    Good To Know

    The quick answers I get asked most about Clacton Airshow. I last checked these on 3 November 2026, so I would still look at the show’s own rules before you go.

    YesCheck firstNo
    1. Pushchairs And BuggiesYesFine on the prom

      It's an open public seafront, so pushchairs come along with no fuss. I would stick to the promenade and the Greensward, as the sand is hard going.

    2. DogsYesOn a lead

      Dogs are welcome on a lead, but not on the beach, apart from guide dogs. With the jet noise and the crowds, I would think hard about whether yours would be happier at home.

    3. Your Own Food And DrinkYesWelcome

      You can bring your own picnic, and the council asks you to use the bins and cut down on single use plastic. Nothing is said about alcohol for the show, and Clacton town centre has a street drinking order, so I would leave it at home to be safe.

    4. Gazebos, Windbreaks And ChairsCheck firstNot confirmed yet

      I haven't seen a rule either way. Chairs and windbreaks are what I see most people bring, and I would ask the show before packing a gazebo, as it blocks the view for everyone behind you.

    5. Water Refill PointsCheck firstNot confirmed yet

      When I last checked there were no refill points listed for the show. I would bring more water than you think you need, as there's very little shade on the front.

    6. Changing Places ToiletYesWest Greensward

      There's a Changing Places toilet next to the West Greensward toilets, with a hoist and changing bench. It needs an entrance key from the council, and a Radar key won't open it, so I would apply well before the show.

    1. Carers' TicketsYesNot needed, it's free

      The whole show is free to watch, so there are no tickets for anyone. In 2026 there was a courtesy shuttle for Blue Badge holders and one carer from the West Road car park.

    2. Hearing SupportCheck firstNot confirmed yet

      I haven't found anything about hearing loops or BSL for the show. I would email the airshow team before you go, and Radio Airshow on Actual Radio carried the commentary in 2026 if that helps.

    3. Quiet AreaCheck firstNot confirmed yet

      There's no calm or sensory space listed. The high ground at Holland on Sea is a quieter place to watch, further from the crowds, and that may work for you.

    4. Re-entryYesFree to come and go

      It's a public seafront with no gates, so you can pop into town and come back. Police searches and vehicle checks were part of the security in 2026, so I would keep your bags light.

    5. First Aid And Lost ChildrenYesOn the seafront

      In 2026 there were first aid points at the Hastings Avenue seafront car park, at Pier Gap and in the middle of the event site. I would pick up a free coloured wristband for each child from a Beach Patrol office or a steward, as it makes reuniting lost children much quicker.

    6. If It RainsCheck firstPack a waterproof

      Unfortunately the weather on the day will be what it will be, so plan accordingly. If it's fresh, dress in layers to keep warm, and the cafés and the pier are close by if a shower rolls in.

    Food & drink

    There are traders and food stalls in the Airshow Village on the West Greensward, plus the cafés, chip shops and pubs in town and on the pier. Queues peak around lunchtime, so I would eat a little earlier or later.

    Kids’ activities

    Children love the RAF careers team, the hands-on and STEM activities in the village, the beach, and the rides and arcades on the pier.

    Toilets

    The West Greensward public toilets are on Marine Parade Way, CO15 1ND, with accessible toilets, baby changing and a Changing Places toilet next door. I would go before the flying starts.

    The beach

    The beach below the Greensward is sand, split up by groynes. I would check the tide times before you set up on it, as high tide leaves far less room.

    Accessibility
    I would suggest the promenade and the Greensward as the easiest places to watch from with a wheelchair or pushchair, as the sand is hard going. The Changing Places toilet next to the West Greensward toilets has a hoist, bed and shower, and you need to apply for an Access Key to use it. In 2026 Blue Badge holders could use the West Road car park, with a courtesy shuttle for them and one carer to the Toby Carvery. When I last checked, the council hadn’t published an accessible viewing area for the show, so I would advise calling Tendring District Council on 01255 686868 before you travel.
    Blue Badge parking
    The town car parks have disabled bays, including 12 at Carnarvon Road and 6 at Wellesley Road, and when I last checked Blue Badge holders could park free for up to three hours at Wellesley Road. Seafront car parks near the display are often closed during the show. Spaces are first come, first served, so I would advise arriving early and checking the council’s car parking page before you go.
    Noise
    Some displays are really loud and can upset people who are sensitive to noise. I would recommend bringing ear defenders for children.
    Drones
    Unauthorised drones aren’t allowed at the event, so please leave yours at home.
    Programme
    The official programme, with the flight times and facts about the aircraft, was £6 in 2026, and you could pick one up at the West Greensward Airshow site. I would pick one up, as it helps fund the free show.
    Supporting the show
    Clacton Airshow is free to watch but costs a lot to put on. I would bring some cash on the day for the bucket collections. There’s more on how to help in .
    Listen live
    In 2026 Radio Airshow was broadcast on Actual Radio across both days. You can ask a smart speaker to play Radio Airshow, or use the Actual Radio app or website. I find it handy for the commentary if you’re away from the crowd centre.
    If the weather turns
    Sea mist, low cloud or strong wind can change the programme or stop some displays. Timings can change for operational reasons or the weather, so I would check the official channels on the morning and pack a waterproof.
